tagline: Out of Lake Placid, past the Cascade Lakes, down Keene Valley.
intro: Route 73 leaves Lake Placid by Cascade Road, past the Olympic ski jumps and the turn for John Brown's farm, climbs to about 2,000 feet and runs along the side of a high ridge by the Cascade Lakes, with Pitchoff Mountain close on the northwest. Then it comes down into Keene and follows the East Branch of the Ausable through Keene Valley and on toward the Northway, with Chapel Pond and Roaring Brook Falls along the way.
The Lake Placid to Keene stretch was the old North West Bay Road. The state ordered it built in 1810, conceded in 1812 that the money was entirely inadequate, and had it finished by 1818.

moments.title: Lake Placid Olympic Ski Jumping Complex
moments.text: Jump towers built for the 1980 Winter Olympics stand where the Lake Placid Club made a ski jump of the bare hillside in 1920.

moments.title: Cascade Mountain
moments.text: A landslide split Long Pond at the mountain's foot after 1860, and in 1878 the two halves were renamed the Cascade Lakes for the waterfall in the slide's path.

moments.title: Keene
moments.text: The town takes in 15 of the 46 High Peaks, Mount Marcy among them, on ground where the bedrock lies so close to the surface that little of it will farm.
